note: Verified status reflects sources checked on 2026-10-23. Re-check vendor docs before implementing each adapter.

categories.name: Frontier model APIs
categories.description: The labs whose own models you call directly. These are the brains your router picks between.

categories.name: Open-weight & regional models
categories.description: Cheaper, often OpenAI-compatible APIs, plus models you can host yourself. Strong for bulk and utility steps.

categories.name: Gateways & clouds
categories.description: One key or one bill reaching many models. Use for fallback, price routing and enterprise buyers.

categories.name: Coding agents
categories.description: Full agents (not just models) that edit repos. Driven headless, by SDK, or as cloud tasks.

categories.name: Hosted agent runtimes
categories.description: Vendor-run sandboxes you send a task to over REST and get results back. Best way to run other labs' agents at scale.

categories.name: Computer-use & browser agents
categories.description: For sites and apps with no API. Slower and riskier, so use only where no API exists.

categories.name: Research & search
categories.description: Deep research agents and search APIs that feed facts and citations to every other agent.

categories.name: General autonomous agents
categories.description: Do-anything agents. Few have real APIs, so most are reachable only through their apps.

categories.name: Image, video, voice & music
categories.description: Specialists the router hands creative sub-tasks to.

categories.name: Design & workspace tools
categories.description: Where outputs land and get edited: design canvases, docs, workspaces.

categories.name: Enterprise agent platforms
categories.description: Company agent stacks that already speak A2A. Your orchestrator can delegate to them, or be delegated to.

categories.name: Protocols & frameworks
categories.description: The plumbing: open protocols to talk to agents, and frameworks to build your own specialist agents.

categories.name: Automation & app hubs
categories.description: Thousands of apps behind one auth layer, so agents can act in Gmail, Slack, CRMs and more.

groq.name: Groq
groq.notes: Prices are per hosted model; see the Groq models page.

together.name: Together AI
together.notes: The model list carries prices when Together publishes them.

claude-managed-agents.name: Claude Managed Agents

settings.label: Environment id
settings.help: A cloud environment to run in; one is created on first use when empty.

pricing.note: Each session reports its list cost (USD cents); a budget cap is sent with the session.

claude-managed-agents.notes: Beta. Not ZDR/HIPAA eligible yet. Output files come through the Files API; there is no structured PR field.

openai-agents.name: OpenAI Agents API

pricing.note: Session usage in tokens at the model's price; hosted sandboxes bill at container rates during active turns.

openai-agents.notes: Public beta since 10 Sep 2026; hosted browser since 29 Sep 2026 asks approval for site access and sign-in. US data residency only, no ZDR.

gemini-managed-agents.name: Gemini managed agents (Interactions API)

pricing.note: Interaction usage in tokens; environment compute is not billed during the preview. Capped with max_total_tokens.

gemini-managed-agents.notes: Managed agents are in public preview; the Interactions API is GA.

jules.name: Jules

settings.label: Repository source
settings.help: A GitHub repository connected to Jules; empty runs without a repository.

pricing.note: Jules reports no cost; runs are bounded by time.

jules.notes: GitHub repositories only. No cancel method; Brio stops following a cancelled session.

devin.name: Devin

pricing.note: Sessions report ACUs consumed; set the agent's USD per ACU to meter them. Capped with max_acu_limit.

devin.notes: v3 API (v1/v2 deprecated). Keys start with cog_. No API to approve a safe-mode action.

pricing.note: Tasks report credits used; set the agent's USD per credit to meter them.

bedrock-agentcore.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime

pricing.note: Runtime usage is billed by AWS (CloudWatch); nothing in the API response. Runs are bounded by time.

bedrock-agentcore.notes: Hosts your own agent; the payload is {"prompt": …} and the reply is the agent's text (SSE or JSON). The key is JSON {accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken?}.

foundry-agents.name: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service

pricing.note: Azure bills the deployment; set a price on the agent to meter tokens.

foundry-agents.notes: Entra auth: the key is JSON {tenantId, clientId, clientSecret} for a service principal. Runs use the Responses API in background mode.

openai-image.name: OpenAI Images

pricing.note: GPT Image 2.5 bills image tokens ($30 per 1M output); there is no flat per-image price, so runs are metered at an estimated $0.20 per image (high quality, 1536 px). Set the agent's USD per image for your size and quality.

openai-image.notes: Synchronous, base64 results. gpt-image-1 shut down 23 Oct 2026; gpt-image-1.5 and -1-mini shut down 1 Dec 2026.

openai-speech.name: OpenAI Speech

pricing.note: tts-1-hd's $30 per 1M characters, the highest rate, as the default; tts-1 is $15 and gpt-4o-mini-tts about $12 per 1M audio tokens.

openai-speech.notes: Every /audio/speech model shuts down on 6 Jan 2027; the replacement is Realtime-only. Voice: options.voice (default alloy). 4,096 characters per call.

gemini-video.name: Gemini Omni video

pricing.note: Omni Flash video is about $0.10 per second at 720p (5,792 output tokens a second at $17.50 per 1M); higher resolutions cost more.

gemini-video.notes: Through the Interactions API. Veo left the Gemini API on 22 Oct 2026 (GA Veo is Vertex-only). Paid tier only.

gemini-image.name: Gemini Nano Banana images

pricing.note: Nano Banana 2.1 is about $0.034 (1K), $0.050 (2K) and $0.113 (4K) per image; metered at the 2K rate.

gemini-image.notes: Through the Interactions API. Imagen shut down 17 Aug 2026.

flux.name: FLUX (BFL API)

pricing.note: BFL reports each job's cost in credits at $0.01 each.

flux.notes: The model is the path. Results are signed URLs that live minutes; Brio downloads them at once. Regional hosts api.eu.bfl.ai and api.us.bfl.ai work as a base URL.

runway.name: Runway API

pricing.note: Tasks report their cost in credits at $0.01 each (gen4.5 is 12 credits a second). Moderated failures are charged.

runway.notes: Ratios and durations are per model; defaults are gen4.5's (1280:720 or 720:1280, 2–10 s). Set options.ratios / options.durations for other models.

luma.name: Luma Agents API

pricing.note: Luma reports no cost. Metered per generation at $0.90 (ray-3.2 720p, 10 s); 5 s is $0.30, 1080p 10 s $3.60, uni-1 images $0.04. Set the agent's USD per generation for what it makes.

luma.notes: The Dream Machine API (ray-2) is legacy. Results are presigned for an hour.

kling.name: Kling API

pricing.note: Charges in billing[] are metered as reported when in US dollars; otherwise by seconds made at $0.168 (kling-v3 pro with audio; 4.0 prices are unpublished).

kling.notes: The model is in the path (/text-to-video/kling-4.0). No free key check: the first run checks the key. China accounts use https://api-beijing.klingai.com.

elevenlabs.name: ElevenLabs text to speech

pricing.note: Billed per character (the character-cost header): $0.08 per 1K for v3, v4 and Multilingual v2; Flash and Turbo are $0.04.

elevenlabs.notes: Voice: options.voiceId (a default library voice otherwise). Regional and data-residency hosts work as a base URL.

ideogram.name: Ideogram API

pricing.note: Metered as reported (usage_cost_usd_micros) when Ideogram returns it, else at an estimated $0.10 per image.

ideogram.notes: Strong at text inside images. Unsafe results come back without a URL.

recraft.name: Recraft API

pricing.note: Each answer reports the API units charged; 1,000 units are $1 (v4.1 is 35 units an image).

recraft.notes: Vector models return SVG. Needs a positive API-unit balance.
